en.title: How to File an e-Return — 2026–27
en.directAnswer: NBR’s e-Return system lets individual taxpayers file online. For 2026–27, use the current NBR portal and notices. Prepare income, asset, expense, tax-payment and withholding information before starting. Read the final return before submission and save the acknowledgement.

atAGlance.whoFor: An individual taxpayer wants a simple filing walkthrough.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Income Tax Act, 2023; Finance Act, 2026; NBR e-Return public notices and forms.
atAGlance.mainRule: NBR launched the 2026–27 individual e-Return system in July 2026. Deadlines and incentives can change, so quote only the current notice.
atAGlance.updateStatus: DYNAMIC DEADLINE: never hard-code a filing deadline or incentive without a dated NBR notice.

en.lawMeaning: NBR launched the 2026–27 individual e-Return system in July 2026. Deadlines and incentives can change, so quote only the current notice. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Sign in to the official e-Return system.
evidence: TIN; salary/income statements; bank information; investment proof; TDS certificates; tax payment challans; asset information.
en.simpleExample: A taxpayer sees a pre-filled tax credit. They should compare it with their own TDS evidence instead of assuming every pre-filled number is correct.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Filing from unofficial link.
Common mistakes: waiting until the last day..

whatIf.question: What if the portal shows an error?
whatIf.answer: Save screenshots and use NBR help channels.

whatIf.question: What if you filed wrong information?
What if you cannot understand a schedule?
whatIf.answer: Get tax help before submitting false data.

en.specialistTrigger: Large assets; business income; foreign income; audit/notice; major data mismatch.
